# p0_aws_iam_federation (Resource)

An AWS IAM Federation installation. Users sign in to one AWS account through a federation app in Okta, PingOne or PingFederate, and P0 grants them access by putting policies on the account's roles and pool roles.

**Important:** Before you create this resource, stage the federation with `p0_aws_iam_federation_staged`, and create P0's role, the SAML provider and the pool roles that it describes. Creating this resource has P0 check that the SAML provider trusts the federation app and that the pool has `pool_size` roles that trust the SAML provider. If a check fails, the apply fails with P0's message.

To have an account's users sign in through the federation, set its `p0_aws_iam_write` login to `type = "aws-iam-federation"` and `federation` to this resource's `id`.

Set every other attribute to the staged resource's value, so that a change to the staged federation replaces this resource too.

Destroying this resource returns the federation to its staged state, which `p0_aws_iam_federation_staged` still owns.

**Note:** This integration is currently in preview.

For the AWS install steps, see [Setting up AWS IAM management](https://docs.p0.dev/integrations/resource-integrations/aws/installation-methods).

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Has AWS account 123456789012 trust the Okta app that the
# p0_okta_aws_iam_federation_app example installs. For a PingOne app, set
# identity_provider to "pingone" and read the p0_pingone_aws_iam_federation_app
# resource instead. For a PingFederate app, set identity_provider to
# "pingfederate" and read the p0_pingfederate_aws_iam_federation_app resource.
resource "p0_aws_iam_federation_staged" "example" {
  id                = "okta-prod"
  account_id        = "123456789012"
  identity_provider = "okta"
  app               = p0_okta_aws_iam_federation_app.example.id
}

data "http" "saml_metadata" {
  url = p0_okta_aws_iam_federation_app.example.saml_metadata_url
}

resource "aws_iam_saml_provider" "p0_federation" {
  name                   = p0_aws_iam_federation_staged.example.saml_provider_name
  saml_metadata_document = data.http.saml_metadata.response_body
}

resource "aws_iam_role" "p0_federation" {
  name               = p0_aws_iam_federation_staged.example.role.name
  assume_role_policy = p0_aws_iam_federation_staged.example.role.trust_policy
}

resource "aws_iam_role_policy" "p0_federation" {
  name   = p0_aws_iam_federation_staged.example.role.name
  role   = aws_iam_role.p0_federation.name
  policy = p0_aws_iam_federation_staged.example.role.inline_policy
}

resource "aws_iam_role" "p0_federation_pool" {
  count = p0_aws_iam_federation_staged.example.pool_size
  name  = format("%s-%d", p0_aws_iam_federation_staged.example.role.name, count.index)
  path  = p0_aws_iam_federation_staged.example.pool.path
  # IAM refuses a trust policy that names a SAML provider that doesn't exist.
  depends_on         = [aws_iam_saml_provider.p0_federation]
  assume_role_policy = p0_aws_iam_federation_staged.example.pool.trust_policy
}

resource "aws_iam_role_policy" "p0_federation_pool_ssh" {
  count  = p0_aws_iam_federation_staged.example.pool_size
  name   = "P0PolicySharedSSH"
  role   = aws_iam_role.p0_federation_pool[count.index].name
  policy = p0_aws_iam_federation_staged.example.pool.ssh_policy
}

resource "p0_aws_iam_federation" "example" {
  id                = p0_aws_iam_federation_staged.example.id
  account_id        = p0_aws_iam_federation_staged.example.account_id
  partition         = p0_aws_iam_federation_staged.example.partition
  pool_size         = p0_aws_iam_federation_staged.example.pool_size
  identity_provider = p0_aws_iam_federation_staged.example.identity_provider
  app               = p0_aws_iam_federation_staged.example.app
  depends_on = [
    aws_iam_role_policy.p0_federation,
    aws_iam_role_policy.p0_federation_pool_ssh,
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `account_id` (String) The ID of the AWS account that users sign in to
- `app` (String) The ID of the installed federation app, in P0's Okta (AWS IAM Federation), PingOne (AWS IAM Federation) or PingFederate (AWS IAM Federation) integration, that the AWS account trusts
- `id` (String) The `id` of the `p0_aws_iam_federation_staged` resource whose install this finishes
- `identity_provider` (String) The identity provider of the federation app: 'okta', 'pingone' or 'pingfederate'

### Optional

- `partition` (String) The AWS partition (aws or aws-us-gov). Defaults to aws if not specified.
- `pool_size` (Number) The number of IAM roles that P0 puts resource grants on. Requests share these roles, so the pool limits how many resource grants can be active at the same time. Defaults to 10.

### Read-Only

- `state` (String) This item's install progress in the P0 application:
	- 'stage': The item has been staged for installation
	- 'configure': The item is available to be added to P0, and may be configured
	- 'installed': The item is fully installed
